analysis:
Both supplied units are BASE-side text excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 797-1053 and 1054-1446). No patch hunks or head text were supplied, so the PR's actual edits are not visible and I cannot cite a changed head line. I found no concrete security regression in this documentation file.

The base excerpts describe security-relevant behavior that other files in the PR must be checked against, especially if the same PR changes code:
- SSD prefix cache (T-041, SEC-035). The changelog says the disk budget is half of available disk, with a 20 GiB write reserve, and that checkpoints are bound to tenant, model, prompt, binary and runtime identity. The T-041 threat definition states a 30-minute sliding TTL (since 2026-09-26). Any head-side change to the TTL or to account scoping needs a fresh SEC-035 sign-off.
- App Attest and legacy MDM serving paths (TB-011, T-052..T-058, A-015..A-017). The changelog mentions shadow-only enrollment and the rule that APNs/MDM stays authoritative.
- Request profiler and fleet snapshots (T-051). Rows are described as prompt-free, with admin export endpoints.
- Provider runtime manifest union (TB-009, T-034). It accepts hashes from every active release.
- Hugging Face model download fallback to R2 with per-file SHA-256 checks (A-004, T-012).
- Stats caching and payouts (TB-008).

Next pass: confirm that changelog claims in the PR match the code and threat-model changes, and look for changelog statements that overclaim security properties.
